en: Having offered praise with incomparable qualities, this hymn—a mere vessel of a few drops—has been composed by me, a dull-witted fool.
I perpetually bow my head with palms joined in reverence to Lokeśvara, the treasury of virtues and the ocean of qualities. || 1 ||

Salutations always to Him whose name is truly meaningful, who flows through the vital breaths, by whom [the world] crosses the waters of the sensory objects, and who protects this world of beings thus afflicted by the sufferings of hunger and thirst. || 2 ||

I bow to you, the embodiment of compassion, whose body possesses a hue like that of a red mark made from the finest saffron, whose form is beautified by the thirty-two marks of a great man, and who possesses a heart of tender affection and compassion for all beings.
O sole Lord of the earth, you alone are the refuge capable of destroying the great abode of the ocean of saṃsāra;
by no one can the multitude of your virtues be counted—[I take refuge in] that Lord of the World whose name is known as Avalokita.

I go for refuge eternally to you, O Lord of the World, whose divine form is adorned with various kinds of ornaments, whose matted locks are graced by the crescent moon, and who holds a mandala in your left hand while granting boons with your right.

I go for refuge to those feet of the Lord of the World, the lotus-feet of you, the Protector, which are surrounded by Brahmā and the others, by hosts of gods and siddhas, and by gandharvas, kinnaras, mahoragas, nāgas, and yakṣas. (6)

I have gone for refuge to those feet of the Lord of the World, which are surrounded by a retinue of spirits—piśācas, garuḍas, uragas, rākṣasīs, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, mahallakas, and the kings of kings—as well as hundreds of vaiśvānaras and asuras. || 7 ||

Just as the ocean does not reach exhaustion even by the rays of the sun, so too this ocean of virtues of yours does not diminish, O Lord of the World, you who are the repository of renowned fame; for the treasure of qualities belonging to an ocean of virtues is never depleted, even by hundreds of masters of poetry.
Those who indeed recite these eight verses every day swiftly attain wealth, sons, and liberation;
they overcome the multitude of diseases such as leprosy and attain forbearance; we bow down deeply at the pair of your feet. 9.
The Eight Verses on the Glorious Noble Avalokiteśvara are complete.
